chapter: Childhood, first drums and the hustling years
title: Pickup band out West, Pierce Arrow burns in New Mexico
summary: A small group led by Roosevelt Thomas of St. Louis went to Colorado and New Mexico, and the promoter's Pierce Arrow burned up, ending the venture.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, what happened after that, after those days of --

Well, after those days here, then I had an opportunity to get West, and so I went to -- with a little group, I went to Colorado. And a fellow had a big car, and -- see, when you put yourself in that era, you were just speculating. Everything was speculation, almost. So this guy

wanted us to go out West, and so we had about a four, five piece band. And he would go out to book some dances and things, and we had a few. And the next thing I know, he had one of those great big Pierce Arrows, at that time, with the headlights on side and all that. And he -- this thing caught afire and burned up. So that left us, so that blew that gig, because without any transportation out in New Mexico, where we were at that particular time, you --

Yeah, we played Colorado, well, this is -- the next state is New Mexico. And then -- so this was like a little territory thing that we were going to try to build up. But nothing really happened behind that.
This was just a pickup group, just a pickup group.
Let's see, a fellow by the name of Roosevelt Thomas, out of St. Louis. And he went out with us, you know.
He was the one that had the Pierce Arrow.
No, another fellow and his wife, yeah. He had the Pierce Arrow and so it was the same type of a deal as I had just left.
